### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via MarketplaceInstallLocalPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **5** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json da46b2afe3e6829dcf70051f10578c61d611ec72` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3fe06cd3f7f2a5bb8e4234ecc9843559eef3d2fd` — the merge of head `365d3ac3cab55c47125879dc62e258396d9216d2` into base `da46b2afe3e6829dcf70051f10578c61d611ec72`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3fe06cd3f7f2a5bb8e4234ecc9843559eef3d2fd && git checkout 3fe06cd3f7f2a5bb8e4234ecc9843559eef3d2fd
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin da46b2afe3e6829dcf70051f10578c61d611ec72 365d3ac3cab55c47125879dc62e258396d9216d2 && git checkout -B drift-repro da46b2afe3e6829dcf70051f10578c61d611ec72 && git merge --no-ff 365d3ac3cab55c47125879dc62e258396d9216d2

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json da46b2afe3e6829dcf70051f10578c61d611ec72
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs da46b2afe3e6829dcf70051f10578c61d611ec72` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `365d3ac3cab55c47125879dc62e258396d9216d2`
Local-runs: probe — `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs --base 0b6a52e8 --head 365d3ac3 --event` with the PR payload, because the payload-less run reports the level axis NOT APPLICABLE and the two declaration lines are read by that gate's own reader (`scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`); nothing was built, tested or re-run
Scope: packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-protocol-handshake.test.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-rehydrate-order.test.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-sample-data-not-loaded.test.ts + packages/metadata-core/src/protocol-handshake.ts (`checkProtocolCompat`, `resolveDeclaredRange`), packages/core/src/hydration-order.ts and packages/core/src/artifact-packages.ts (`orderHydrationBatch`, `artifactPackageId`, `declaredDependencyIds`), packages/cloud-connection/src/local-manifest-source.ts (`read`/`readAll` shape-free), packages/cli/src/commands/package/install.ts (the lifted body, :172–174)

Face: narrowing (`record-recognisers --paths` on the five committed paths decides no schema or governed face; the changeset's `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line decides, so `--face narrowing`, CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER). Scope floor on this face = every diff path outside the prose faces; the changeset `.changeset/28604-install-local-rehydrate-lifted-entry.md` is the seat's ACCEPT, read here only for ②. Reviewed at 2026-11-01T13:36Z against merge-base `0b6a52e8a0d9982ede44a74912e917b353154582` (= `origin/main`). PR author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; PR is draft. Card #28604 (p3, triage 6557784727, claim 6557844083), order `pm-orders/server/order-28604.md`, os-dev-report 6558578887, source card #28535 / PR #28603 (`7449e479`) all read.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **One flatten, one handshake — holds.** Both judged reads call the existing `flattenPackageBody` (:622) and the existing `checkProtocolCompat` imported from `@objectstack/metadata-core` (:197): rehydrate :1109 `checkProtocolCompat(flattenPackageBody(entry.manifest))`, doors :3863 the same inside `refuseProtocolIncompatibleEntry`. No new flatten function, no inline `{ ...manifest, ...sections }`, no second compat predicate. Base held exactly two `checkProtocolCompat(entry.manifest)` reads; head rewrites those two and adds none. The door-side judge being separate from the boot-side judge is the pre-existing #21834 design (an entry another runtime ledgered after this boot), not a second handshake introduced here.
2. **Outcome parity for a lifted entry with an excluded range — holds.** The flattened view `{ ...meta, ...sections }` carries `engines` from the nested manifest and `id`/`version` from the lifted top (the CLI sets them from `artifact.manifest.id ?? artifact.id`, `install.ts:172`, so they equal the nested ones). `resolveDeclaredRange` then reads `engines.protocol` exactly as for a flat entry; the diagnostic's `packageId` is the same id; `reportProtocolIncompatibleEntry` prints from `entry.manifestId`/`entry.version` and the diagnostic; `refusedAtRehydrate` is keyed by `manifestId`+`installedAt`; the doors answer the shared `protocolIncompatibleAnswer`. Nothing in the refusal path reads the body's shape after the judge. The tests pin this as byte equality against a flat entry on a fresh ledger (error line; reseed and purge payloads) and assert the `notLoaded { code, requiredRange }` marker. Red on base (5/37) and three ablation legs reported in the PR; both lit controls pass on both trees.
3. **Compatible lifted entries unchanged — holds.** The load path is untouched: `convertPackageBodyForward(ctx, entry.manifest)` (:1131) still converts and registers the ledgered body unflattened, as base did; only the judge (:1109), the order (:1186) and the doors' judge (:3863) read the flattened view. Lit control asserts the registered manifest deep-equals the ledgered lifted body, no error line, one sync. Ordering of a compatible lifted entry without nested `dependencies` is unchanged: `declaredIds` is empty on both trees and `artifactPackageId` reads the same lifted `id` (sections win in the flatten), so no edge is added and `orderHydrationBatch` keeps source order where no edge decides.
4. **`!isPlainObject(body)` guard — no existing caller moves.** Three pre-existing callers: `normalizeBundle` (:1577) already guards with `isPlainObject(m)` before calling, so the new branch is unreachable from the install door; :3274 `flattenPackageBody(converted)` and :3452 `flattenPackageBody(manifest)` sit past the id gate and the handshake on the install body, which is a non-null object there (an array body read `[].manifest` as undefined on base and is returned as-is on both trees). The guard only changes `null`/primitive inputs, which base threw a TypeError on and which no existing caller can pass. Signature unchanged (a plain-object record in and out). For the new ledger callers the dev measured null/string/number `manifest` values byte-identical on base and head, consistent with the code: `null` still throws inside `checkProtocolCompat` (pre-existing, per-entry caught as "rehydrate failed"); a string/number reads no range and loads as before.
5. **The dependency-order leg — justified, in scope, not a new behaviour.** `inDependencyOrder` (:1182) now reads `flattenPackageBody(entry.manifest)` so a lifted entry's nested `dependencies` (and a lifted multi-package artifact's `packages[]`, which sits at the top in both shapes) feed ADR-0141 D5's ordering. No dependency CHECK runs at boot — `checkDeclaredDependencies` is called once, in `handleInstall` :1798, and AGENTS.md *Startup registry reads* forbids a boot-time verdict — so "ordering" is the whole of what a flat entry's `dependencies` do at boot, and the card's reach names "or whose `dependencies` it does not satisfy". It is the third decision at the rehydrate that reads a manifest key, judged through the same one flatten, with its own red case and ablation leg (lifted module listed ahead of its parent now registers after it). It does not touch the accept set and is not part of the declared narrowing; it is correctly left out of the `Clause-②` line.
6. **Narrowing arm — right, and the carriers are consistent.** An entry that loaded at boot no longer loads, and two served doors move 200 → 422 for it: not a widening, breaking → `no (narrowing)` (#16421), the same reading #28603 declared for the install door. `clause2-line.mjs` reads both the PR body and the changeset as `declared / no / narrowing` and `Metadata-protocol: none`; no authorable key is added, narrowed or re-meant, so `none` and `patch` follow ruling A (AGENTS.md step 3: "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition"). The probe run of `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` with the PR payload: ✓ no major, ✓ level axis (patch · none · narrowing), ✓ lockstep. Title `fix(cloud-connection)!:` on the PR and on the changeset summary (carrier 3), `**BREAKING**` banner in both bodies (carrier 2), exactly one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker in the changeset; the body carries no FROM → TO or consumer-rewrite instruction (the named remedies are the existing refusal's own text), so the category is honest under the gate's statement-against-statement check. `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` could not run here (no `tsx` without `pnpm install`); it is read from the head's check-runs (`Lint · docs & code guards`, in progress at review time) — #28603 carried the identical disposition and landed green. `Skills-docs: none — REASON` is present in the PR body, as the arm owes (SKILL.md:313), and the cited `skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md` sentence does describe this refusal.
7. **Overlap with #28565 — none.** #28565 is an open card with no PR yet (search: the only open PRs naming the plugin file are this one, #28671 whose file list does not include it, and #26517 version packages). Its target check lands in `handleInstall` beside the dependency check (≈:1790–1810, "at both install doors"). This diff's four hunks are :609–626 (`flattenPackageBody` docblock + guard), :1102–1109 (rehydrate judge), :1181–1189 (`inDependencyOrder`), :3849–3863 (`refuseProtocolIncompatibleEntry`): none inside `handleInstall`, none in its early checks, and `flattenPackageBody`'s signature is unchanged, so a later caller there is unaffected. No textual or semantic conflict foreseen.
8. **Upgrade / availability — no new boot-stop.** The refusal is `continue` inside the per-entry `try` (:1110–1120), identical to the flat path #21762 established: the entry is skipped, the boot proceeds, the ledger is kept, DELETE and a compatible reinstall act on it. No new throw: the flatten is total, `checkProtocolCompat` is pure over objects, and the only throwing input (`manifest: null`) threw on base too and is per-entry caught. A lifted entry whose nested `manifest` is null or whose range is unparsable still loads (no-range / unparsed-range admit on both trees). What an operator sees after upgrading: a pre-fix CLI install built for another protocol is absent, named once in the error log with the remedy, and marked `notLoaded` in the listing — the declared narrowing, not an outage.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/cloud-connection: patch` with `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` + `Metadata-protocol: none`, `!` title and `**BREAKING**` banner in PR body and changeset, one ADR-0087 marker. Consistent with ruling A and with the gate's own reading (probe above). Correct.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions: []`. Two `out_of_scope_findings`, both `carrier: none · noted, not filed`: (a) a ledger file with `manifest: null` throws from `checkProtocolCompat` at the rehydrate (caught, "rehydrate failed") and out of the reseed/purge handlers — verified pre-existing and byte-identical on base; no producer writes it; not filing is acceptable, the seat may file at its discretion; (b) the #28565 overlap note — answered in ①.7.
- Author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`: no login note owed.
- CI at review time: 13 check-runs `success` (Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Dogfood Regression Gate, Test UI, Build-plan and labels), 19 `in_progress` (Build Core, Test Core 1–8, Type Check ×4, Lint ×4, Live E2E UI), 0 failed. The landing pre-check ② (all green) is the seat's at landing; nothing here waives it.
- Non-blocking note: the flatten gives top-level sections precedence over nested meta, so a lifted entry that also carried a top-level `engines` would be judged by the top-level one. No producer (`install.ts` lifts only `id`/`version`) writes that, and it is the install door's own precedence, so parity holds. Not a must-fix.

### ④ Design judgment

On the narrowing face, against the published contract on `main`: ADR-0087 D1 puts the handshake "before loading a package's metadata" at the loader and the installer, with "in range → load, major-incompatible → fail fast with a structured diagnostic"; `skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md` teaches that the runtime "refuses an out-of-range app at the boundary". No page or schema declares a ledgered CLI install as an exception. The narrowing therefore makes the spec's own refusal real at the one boundary where it was silently skipped, and takes no declared capability away from a consumer; the remedy the refusal names (a build for this protocol, or DELETE) is the existing diagnostic's. Per `hits` file: the plugin change holds against the cited `checkProtocolCompat`/`resolveDeclaredRange` (engines read off the flattened view), `orderHydrationBatch`/`artifactPackageId`/`declaredDependencyIds` (ids and dependencies read off the same view), the shape-free `LocalManifestSource` (which is why the total guard is needed) and the CLI body builder (the lifted shape the tests reproduce is the real one). The three test files pin the accepted scenario — byte parity with the flat entry, listing marker, lit controls, dependency order — on the harnesses the flat cases already use. The design holds.
